title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

reading.body:
This is a permitting and compliance failure at the physical plant of a data center, not a failure of any model or software. The 62 natural gas generators at the Vineland site were installed and operated without permits, which is the condition the Air Pollution Control Act exists to enforce. The failure sits in the power layer of the deployment, the part that keeps a campus running when the grid cannot, and it was present before any computing workload depended on it.

Catching it required a permit review before installation, or an inspection before the generators were run. State inspectors did find the generators in late July, and the fine followed in September. The noise complaints point to a second channel that was already open: nearby homeowners had sued over persistent noise, and the Cumberland County Health Department had issued violation orders for excessive noise, so the site's effects on its surroundings were being reported by neighbours independently of the permit question.

What is not established is intent, and the reporting does not describe any AI system or AI decision. The homeowners' suit is an allegation, not a verdict, and the article does not say what happens next. The record also does not establish whether the generators were running to serve existing workloads or to prepare for the campus's scheduled completion at the end of the year.

reports.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

summary:
New Jersey fined DataOne $1.07 million on Tuesday after state inspectors found 62 natural gas generators at its Vineland data center site in late July. The 2,000 kilowatt generators, each about the size of a tractor trailer, lacked permits to be installed or operated. Officials said the penalty for violating the Air Pollution Control Act is the largest ever issued to a data center operator in New Jersey. Gov. Mikie Sherrill said such projects must benefit New Jersey communities.

The planned data center campus is 2.6 million square feet and would need 350 megawatts, enough for a medium size city. It is scheduled for completion at the end of the year, and some parts are already in use. Nearby homeowners have sued DataOne over persistent noise, and the Cumberland County Health Department has issued violation orders for excessive noise. The article does not say what happens next.
